sections.label: Budget cut for Head N
sections.summary: A motion is moved to reduce the total sum allocated for Head N of the Estimates by $100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head N of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Singapore is a small country, but one which has punched well above its weight on the international stage because we have made ourselves relevant to others and built up trust and credibility over the years since our independence.

sections.label: Trans-Pacific Partnership signing
sections.summary: The TPP was signed by many countries including Japan and the US, but still needs domestic ratification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The recent high point of this integration is the signing of the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP).

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Many countries have come together for this, including Japan and the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This is potentially a huge opportunity for all parties as two-thirds of world trade, or about $1.6 trillion, take place in this region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, the TPP still needs to be ratified in the domestic legislatures before it comes into force.

sections.label: Tribunal jurisdiction ruling
sections.summary: The Tribunal has ruled it has jurisdiction to hear the case, and the hearing on the merits will proceed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In an important development, the Tribunal has now ruled it has jurisdiction to hear the case, and the hearing on the merits will proceed.

sections.label: North Korea nuclear testing
sections.summary: North Korea carried out its fourth nuclear test in January 2016 and issues statements about potential strikes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: North Korea has continued its nuclear testing, carrying out its fourth test in January 2016, and is issuing regular statements about a potential strike against Seoul and Washington.

sections.label: Singapore ties with Koreas
sections.summary: Singapore is one of the few countries with diplomatic ties to both North Korea and South Korea.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore is one of the few countries that have diplomatic ties with both North Korea and South Korea.

sections.label: Terror attacks and arrests
sections.summary: Brussels and Paris attacks conveyed no one is safe, and arrests continue in Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The terrorist attacks in Brussels and Paris have captured the international imagination, conveying the message that nobody is safe anywhere in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Arrests continue to be made in Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia of individuals who have been involved with international terrorist organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While we need a strong defence and Home Team, I believe that it is also important to work with neighbours in a collaborative fashion to help alleviate the difficult security situations.

sections.label: China-Japan-US relations affect Singapore
sections.summary: The state of trilateral relations among China, Japan and the US will significantly affect Singapore, the region and beyond.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The state of trilateral relations among China, Japan and the US will significantly affect Singapore, the region and beyond.

sections.label: Question on trilateral relations and oil
sections.summary: The Member asks the Minister about the China-Japan-US relationship amid a slowing economy, US leadership change, and East Asia implications, noting crude oil averaged under US$50 per barrel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Chairman, I would like to ask the Minister if he sees the trilateral China-Japan-US relationship evolving in the light of a slowing economy, and also, if there were a change in the leadership in the US, in particular, what implications would this evolving US-China relationship have on East Asia and Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Crude oil has, over the last year, averaged less than US$50 per barrel, a far cry from, say, 2011 and 2014's average price of more than US$95 per barrel.

sections.label: Reaching 622 million customers
sections.summary: Instead of selling to 5.5 million, there is now a chance to reach 622 million potential customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Instead of selling to the 5.5 million, we now have the chance to reach out to 622 million potential customers instead.

sections.label: Community projects Singapore's interests
sections.summary: If played right, the Community will let Singapore project national interests with the grouping's voice, achieving greater outcomes than alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: If we play our cards right, the Community will allow Singapore to project our national interests with the voice of the entire grouping, achieving far greater outcomes than we could alone.

sections.label: South China Sea tensions in 2016
sections.summary: Tensions in the South China Sea worsened in 2016, shown by China's air defence unit deployment on Woody Island during the ASEAN-US Summit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the tensions in the South China Sea appear to have taken a turn for the worse in 2016, manifested most acutely by the timing of China's deployment of an air defence unit on the disputed Woody Island, precisely when the inaugural ASEAN-US Summit in the US was taking place earlier in February this year.

sections.label: Ministry proposes CUES as coordinator
sections.summary: The Ministry began work as coordinator, proposing a Code for Unplanned Encounters at Sea, in the spirit of Singapore's honest broker reputation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, the Ministry has wasted no time in getting down to work as coordinator, proposing a Code for Unplanned Encounters at Sea (CUES), in the spirit of Singapore's reputation on this matter as an honest broker and its reputation as a constructive player in the international arena.

sections.label: South China Sea DOC progress
sections.summary: Asks what progress has been made on fully implementing the DOC and whether China's position on it has changed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, what progress has been made on the full implementation of the Declaration of Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea (DOC), including cooperative projects between ASEAN and China?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What is China's position on the DOC currently and has it changed, given that it has previously stressed that the DOC should precede COC, even if ASEAN's position is that both are not sequential and can be addressed together?

sections.label: Singapore-US relations update
sections.summary: Asks the Minister to update the House on relations with the US, future cooperation and challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Could the Minister update the House on the current state of our relations with the US and future areas of bilateral cooperation and support and what, if any, are the challenges going forward?

sections.label: China outbound investment 2015
sections.summary: China's outbound direct investment surpassed inbound FDI for the first time in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: China's outbound direct investment surpassed inbound FDI for the first time in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: At the Inaugural Lancang-Mekong Cooperation Leaders' Meeting on the sidelines of the Boao Forum, Premier Li Keqiang offered preferential loans of 10 billion yuan and credit lines of US$10 billion to five ASEAN countries along the Mekong River to fund infrastructure and improve connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Singapore enjoys good relations with China and celebrated 25 years of diplomatic relations last year with the upgrade of the CSSFTA, an agreement to develop a third govenrment-to-government project in Chongqing.

sections.label: Singapore-Japan relations and JSEPA
sections.summary: Relations with Japan have grown; JSEPA was Japan's first FTA and Singapore's first with a major trading partner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Our relations with Japan have grown and are increasingly broad and multi-faceted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I recall that the Japan-Singapore Economic Partnership Agreement (JSEPA) was Japan's first Free Trade Agreement and Singapore's first with a major trading partner.

sections.label: Singapore-India Strategic Partnership signing
sections.summary: During a landmark visit, Singapore and India elevated relations by signing a Strategic Partnership.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: During the landmark visit, Singapore and India further elevated bilateral relations with the signing of the Strategic Partnership by both Prime Ministers.

sections.label: PM Lee Australia trip
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee will soon travel to Australia to forge new agreements, including enhanced defence cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lee will soon be making a trip to Australia, and, as I understand, it is to forge new agreements, including to enhance our defence cooperation.

sections.label: Singapore-Australia diplomatic relations history
sections.summary: Diplomatic relations with Australia date back to 1941, and Singapore was one of Canberra's earliest foreign posts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In fact, our diplomatic relations with Australia date back to 1941 and we were one of the very earliest foreign posts set up by the Canberra government.

sections.label: Singapore-Malaysia connectivity projects
sections.summary: Open dialogue is needed to manage issues without harming bilateral relations, with progress on the High Speed Rail and Rapid Transit System link.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We must maintain an open dialogue and manage these issues without adversely affecting the overall bilateral relations.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: I observe that enhancing connectivity between Singapore and Malaysia has been a theme in recent years, with progress being made on key bilateral projects, such as the High Speed Rail (HSR) and the Rapid Transit System (RTS) link.

sections.label: Singapore-Indonesia economic ties
sections.summary: Singapore has maintained good economic ties with Indonesia and continued to be its largest foreign investor.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For Indonesia, we have maintained our good economic ties and have continued to be Indonesia's largest foreign investor.

sections.label: Myanmar 2015 elections
sections.summary: General elections took place in Myanmar in November 2015 and the new NLD government was recently sworn in.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In Myanmar, the general elections took place in November 2015 and the new NLD government was recently sworn in.

sections.label: Europe migration and security challenges
sections.summary: Europe faces a large migration wave, heightened security risks after terrorist attacks, and internal challenges including the Greek debt crisis and possible UK exit.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Europe is currently going through a difficult time.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: It is facing one of the largest waves of migration in recent years, with more than a million people entering its borders.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The European Union (EU) is struggling to find solutions to manage the escalating migrant and refugee crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: On top of this, Europe faces heightened security risks in the wake of the recent spate of terrorist attacks in France, Belgium and Turkey.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The EU is also struggling with pressing internal challenges, particularly the Greek debt crisis and the possible exit of the UK, which could paralyse the EU decision-making process.

sections.label: Overseas missions lean teams
sections.summary: Singapore has about 50 overseas missions to-date, which generally operate on very lean teams.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Even though we have about 50 overseas missions to-date, I note that, for good reasons, our missions generally operate on very lean teams.

sentences.text: Last year, radicalised Bangladeshis were discovered in Singapore.

sentences.text: In May last year, ISIS cited Singapore as a possible target, along with the Philippines and USA.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: The year 2015 was also a landmark for the UN, with the adoption of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

sentences.text: The Budget Book reveals that MFA's focus has been placed, in part, on sustainable development this year, particularly through the Singapore Cooperation Programme.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I invite MFA today to outline its initiatives on how we can put ourselves on the map, as far as the sustainable development goals and sustainable development as a whole goes, with particular reference to our Sustainable Development and Climate Change (SDCC) programme.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This was unveiled last year after the September Summit.

sections.label: Cyclical posting regime for FSOs

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The cyclical posting regime is one in which families of FSOs need to relocate on a three- to four-year cycle as a result of an overseas posting.

sections.label: US-China relationship key variable

sentences.text: The state of the United States (US)-China relationship is the key variable.

sections.label: China's rise shifts strategic balance

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: China's emergence as a rising power has shifted the strategic balance.

sections.label: China's South China Sea activities
sections.summary: In the South China Sea, China has conducted reclamation works, built runways and port facilities, and deployed military assets on disputed features.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In the South China Sea, China has conducted extensive reclamation works, constructed runways and port facilities, and it has deployed significant military assets on disputed features in the South China Sea.

sections.label: Rising power economic interdependence
sections.summary: Economic interdependence between a rising power and an existing super power prevents all-out confrontation because the economic impact on both would be too high.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Despite their differences, there is one point worth noting, which is that never before in history has a rising power, in its engagement with an existing super power, had such an unprecedented level of economic interdependence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And this means that they cannot embark on an all-out confrontation because the economic impact on both states will be too high.

sections.label: DPRK missile launches
sections.summary: Recent provocative missile launches by the DPRK are unsettling and clearly violate UN Security Council resolutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The recent spate of provocative missile launches in the last few months by the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) has been unsettling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: They are in clear violation of United Nations (UN) Security Council resolutions.

sections.label: Nuclear DPRK regional tensions
sections.summary: A nuclear-capable, unpredictable and unstable DPRK could prompt Japan and ROK to go nuclear, raising regional tensions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: A nuclear-capable and unpredictable, unstable DPRK could also prompt countries like Japan and ROK to go nuclear and this will further raise tensions in the region.

sections.label: Southeast Asians fighting for ISIS

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: More than 1,000 men and women from Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines and even Singapore are believed to have travelled to the Middle East to fight for ISIS.

sections.label: EU-Singapore Free Trade Agreement
sections.summary: The EUSFTA is the first free trade agreement between an ASEAN country and the EU.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The EU-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (EUSFTA) is the first free trade agreement (FTA) between an ASEAN country and the EU.

sections.label: ASEAN Economic Community integration
sections.summary: The AEC will integrate ASEAN into a single regional market with freer flows of goods, services, investments, skilled labour and capital.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: AEC will integrate and transform ASEAN into a single regional market with a freer flow of goods, services, investments, skilled labour and capital.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: With 620 million people, a labour force that is the third largest in the world, and an estimated gross domestic product (GDP) of US$2.5 trillion, our AEC has huge potential.

sections.label: ASEAN haze-free vision 2020
sections.summary: Leaders endorsed the vision of a haze-free ASEAN by 2020 on transboundary haze pollution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: For instance, on transboundary haze pollution, our Leaders have already endorsed the vision of a haze-free ASEAN by 2020.

sections.label: ASEAN-China FTA upgrade protocol
sections.summary: ASEAN and China signed a protocol last year to upgrade the ASEAN-China Free Trade Agreement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: ASEAN and China signed a protocol last year to upgrade the ASEAN-China Free Trade Agreement (ACFTA), and this will serve to further deepen ASEAN-China economic cooperation and integration.

sections.label: DOC and COC implementation
sections.summary: ASEAN and China should work towards full implementation of the DOC and early conclusion of the COC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: It is thus important to maintain open dialogue on issues of mutual concern to prevent contentious issues from overshadowing the overall ASEAN-China relationship.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We believe that ASEAN and China should remain committed to working towards the full and effective implementation of the Declaration on the Conduct of Parties (DOC) in the South China Sea, as well as the early conclusion of the Code of Conduct (COC).

sections.label: COC outline and issues papers
sections.summary: Both sides agreed to a paper on a possible COC outline and a discussion paper on crucial issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have also had productive and frank discussions on COC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have agreed to a paper on the "List of Elements of the Possible Outline of a COC", and to a discussion paper on the "List of Crucial and Complex Issues" in the drafting of COC.

sections.label: No first use of force
sections.summary: Support was expressed for Vietnam's no first use of force proposal, while China signed the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: As for the "no first use of force", a proposal raised by Vietnam sometime earlier, we have expressed support for this proposal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, China has signed on to the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation which commits all parties to refrain from the threat or the use of force.

sections.label: China-Singapore FTA upgrade
sections.summary: Both sides agreed to a comprehensive and substantive upgrade of the China-Singapore FTA by year end.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Both sides have agreed to achieve a comprehensive and substantive upgrade of the China-Singapore FTA by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Not only is China our largest trading partner, we have also been China's top foreign investor since 2013.

sections.label: India-Singapore Strategic Partnership cooperation
sections.summary: The 2015 India-Singapore Strategic Partnership enables cooperation in finance, civil aviation, urban solutions and skills development, with new initiatives in Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The signing of the India-Singapore Strategic Partnership in November 2015 laid the foundation for us to step up cooperation in diverse areas, including finance, civil aviation, urban solutions and skills development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We hope to create more opportunities for our companies through new initiatives, which include the master-planning of Andhra Pradesh's new capital city and providing support for the Centre of Excellence for Tourism Training in Rajasthan.

sections.label: RCEP negotiations and Australia collaboration
sections.summary: Singapore participates in RCEP negotiations, welcomes commitment to conclude by this year, and foresees collaboration with Australia in many areas if successful.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: It is also actively participating in the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), which is the other big trading bloc which we are working on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We welcome the commitment by all RCEP countries to intensify efforts to conclude the negotiations by this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In fact, right now, or over the next couple of weeks, we are in the final stages of negotiations and, if we are successful, we will see unprecedented levels of collaboration and engagement with Australia in diverse areas, including economic integration, investments in new growth areas like food and agribusiness, aquaculture, tourism, enhanced defence arrangements, further collaboration and engagement on foreign affairs, further joint-work and innovation, research and development (R&D), arts and culture, and people-to-people exchanges.

sections.label: Singapore G20 participation and Hangzhou invitation
sections.summary: Singapore is not a G20 member but contributed when invited, and China has invited Singapore to the Hangzhou Summit this September.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Whilst we are not a member of G20, we contributed actively when invited to participate, and, most recently, Singapore has been invited by China to attend the Hangzhou Summit this September.

sections.label: Kuala Lumpur-Singapore HSR and RTS progress
sections.summary: Progress is being made on the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail and the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System Link.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Progress is being made on the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail and the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System Link.

sections.label: Singapore-Indonesia investment and haze cooperation

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are the largest investor in China, we are the largest investor in Indonesia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have some US$5.9 billion invested in Indonesia last year, and we are Indonesia's third largest trading partner, as well as each other's largest source of tourists.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: For instance, SembCorp is developing a 2,700 hectare industrial park in Kendal, Semarang.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Year after year, the main victims of this haze are not Singaporeans; it is actually the Indonesians themselves, who live at ground zero.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: So, we want to do more with the Indonesian government and other interested stakeholders to promote sustainable agricultural practices, to strengthen our response to forest fires and to hold errant companies responsible for the fires that they start or allow to occur on their concession areas.

sections.label: MFA voted best employer for training
sections.summary: MFA was voted by students at four local universities as Best Employer in Singapore for Training and Development in 2016 in Universum's survey.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: On this note, I was gratified that MFA was recently voted by the students at our four local universities, that is, the National University of Singapore, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore Management University and Singapore Institute of Management as the "Best Employer in Singapore for Training and Development in 2016" in Universum's "100 Most Attractive Employers in Singapore" survey.

sections.label: Singapore as price taker

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Whatever happens, we have to remember that we are price takers, we are not price makers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)

sentences.text: About two million Chinese tourists visit Singapore each year and close to a million Singaporeans visited China in 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: China is Singapore's largest trading partner and we have been China's top foreign investor since 2013, a point which Minister Vivian highlighted.

sections.label: Chongqing Connectivity Initiative project
sections.summary: After the Suzhou Industrial Park and Tianjin Eco-City, China asked Singapore to launch a third Government-to-Government project in Western China, the Chongqing Connectivity Initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Following the success of the Suzhou Industrial Park (SIP) and the Sino-Singapore Tianjin Eco-City (SSTEC) projects, the Chinese approached Singapore to launch a third Government-to-Government project in Western China.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This third G-to-G project, known as the Chongqing Connectivity Initiative (CCI), is based on the theme of "modern connectivity and modern services".

sections.label: Japan honours Lee Kuan Yew
sections.summary: The Japanese Cabinet decided to confer a posthumous award, the Grand Cordon of the Order of the Paulownia Flowers, on Mr Lee Kuan Yew.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Japanese Cabinet has decided to confer a posthumous award, the Grand Cordon of the Order of the Paulownia Flowers, on Mr Lee Kuan Yew.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This would be the first time the award has been given posthumously to a foreign individual.

sections.label: Award elevated to own class
sections.summary: Since the award became a class of its own in 2003, only four foreign personalities have received it.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since the award was elevated to a class of its own in 2003, only four foreign personalities have received it.

sections.label: EU trade and investment in Singapore
sections.summary: The EU is Singapore's third largest trading partner and largest investor, with around 11,000 companies registered here.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The EU is Singapore's third largest trading partner and the largest investor in Singapore, with around 11,000 companies registered here.

sections.label: SkillsFuture learning from Germany
sections.summary: As part of SkillsFuture, Singapore is keen to learn from Germany's best practices in vocational training.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As part of the SkillsFuture initiative, we are keen to learn from Germany's best practices in vocational training.

sections.label: Trade with emerging markets growth
sections.summary: Trade between Singapore and emerging markets excluding China and Southeast Asia grew from about S$130 billion in 2010 to over S$160 billion in 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In 2010, total trade between Singapore and emerging markets, excluding China and Southeast Asia, stood at about S$130 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: By 2014, this trade had grown to more than S$160 billion.

sections.label: Singapore trade agreements with EAEU and Turkey
sections.summary: Tharman and Shuvalov agreed to review the 1966 USSR Trade Agreement as a new FTA with the EAEU, and the Turkey-Singapore FTA was signed in November 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For example, Deputy Prime Minister Tharman and Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Igor Shuvalov agreed last year to review the Trade Agreement signed between Singapore and the former Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) in 1966.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This will take the form of a new FTA between Singapore and the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), which comprises Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, the Kyrgyz Republic and Russia.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In November 2015, we signed the Turkey-Singapore FTA (TRSFTA), a significant milestone for both countries.

sections.label: Singapore welcomes French conference initiative
sections.summary: Singapore welcomes the latest French initiative to convene an international conference seeking a political solution to the stalled Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore welcomes the latest French initiative to convene an international conference to seek a political solution to the stalled Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

sections.label: Training Palestinian officials, assistance package
sections.summary: Singapore has trained over 230 Palestinian officials in 20 years and since 2013 offered a S$5 million technical assistance package for Palestinian capacity building.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Over the last 20 years, we have trained over 230 Palestinian officials in various courses under the Singapore Cooperation Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Further, since 2013, Singapore has also offered a special technical assistance package valued at S$5 million to support Palestinian capacity building.

sections.label: FTA with GCC
sections.summary: The FTA with the GCC will help further economic cooperation with its six members.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Our FTA with the GCC will help further economic cooperation with its six members.

sections.label: Singapore-Africa trade and forums
sections.summary: Singapore-Africa trade grew 10% annually over the last decade, and MFA will host a ministerial visit and business forum to foster partnerships.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In the last decade, trade between Singapore and Africa has grown by an average of 10% annually, with total investments in Sub-Saharan Africa exceeding S$21.1 billion in 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Good relations with the respective governments can help open doors for our companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This August, MFA will host the Second Sub-Saharan Africa High-Level Ministerial Exchange Visit that aims to foster closer political partnerships with key African leaders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The Fourth Africa-Singapore Business Forum will build on past editions that had attracted about 2,000 participants from Africa and the region to explore business opportunities and establish networks.

sections.label: SCP participant milestone
sections.summary: The SCP reached its 100,000th participant in July last year, with more than 170 developing countries having participated to date.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Notably, the SCP reached a milestone with our 100,000th participant in July last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To date, more than 170 developing countries have participated in the SCP.

sections.label: Foreign officials learn sustainable development
sections.summary: Almost 11,000 foreign officials have learnt from Singapore's sustainable development journey through the SCP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To Asst Prof Mohan's query, almost 11,000 foreign officials have learnt from our sustainable development journey through the SCP.

sections.label: Nepal evacuation and consular readiness
sections.summary: Without a mission in Nepal, Singapore brought home 70 Singaporeans and seven Permanent Residents, and MFA runs exercises and 24-hour officer rosters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Although we have no Singapore Mission in Nepal, we persisted with a whole-of-Government spirit and worked with the Nepalese government to bring home 70 Singaporeans and seven Permanent Residents safely.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To maintain a high level of readiness, MFA regularly conducts simulation and training exercises and reviews of our contingency plans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We and our Overseas Missions have rostered officers 24 hours a day so that Singaporeans in need of urgent help can get in touch with MFA.

sections.label: Contacting Singaporeans after Paris attacks
sections.summary: Officers worked day and night until all 263 registered Singaporeans in the Paris terror attacks were accounted for.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: During the Paris terror attacks last November, our officers worked day and night to contact our e-registrants.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We did not stop until every 263 registered Singaporeans were accounted for.

sections.label: Adaptive approach to diplomatic relations
sections.summary: Singapore adapts to each country's circumstances and has no current plans to appoint cultural liaison officers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The way in which we go about it is to be adaptive and to be cognisant of the unique circumstances in every country and region that we establish diplomatic relations with.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There are no plans currently for specifically appointing cultural liaison officers.

sections.label: ASEAN consensus and dispute mechanisms
sections.summary: A dispute resolution and regulatory mechanism is the minimum, but ASEAN works by consensus so all must agree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I do not think we need all of that, but the minimum is some kind of dispute resolution and regulatory mechanism.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Certainly, as the pace and scope of integration proceeds, there will be need for more institutional arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I just want to caution that ASEAN works by consensus, so, we would have to make sure that everyone agrees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Many of the Middle Eastern countries would require something like US$80-plus, say, for Iran or Iraq to come out break even for their national budget.

sections.label: Saudi oil production cost
sections.summary: The Saudi Foreign Minister said the true cost of a barrel of oil is between US$2 and US$5.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I asked the Saudi Arabian Foreign Minister and the Saudi Arabian Minister for Energy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I asked him, "What is the cost of getting a barrel of oil from Saudi Arabia?" He said, "Well, the true cost, the real cost to us, depending on whose accounting standard is used, is somewhere between US$2-US$5 per barrel." That is the cost of lifting oil out from Saudi Arabia, which means everything else is plus, plus.

sections.label: Oil producers facing budget squeeze
sections.summary: Many countries, especially Middle East oil producers and some in the region, face a significant budgetary squeeze.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Many countries, especially oil producers in the Middle East, and including some in our own region, now have to come to terms with a very significant budgetary squeeze.

sections.label: Singapore's energy and budget principles
sections.summary: Singapore should not subsidise energy, must pay full international prices, and avoid rosy projections causing panic.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The domestic implication of that for Singapore is the following: (a) we have never subsidised energy and we should not do so; (b) whether it comes to utilities, transport and all those other things, we must always be prepared to pay the full international price, whether it is high or low; (c) we must make sure our economy continues to be built on sustainable, sensible, rational economic principles; and (d) when we have debates on Budgets like this, examine people's assumptions and make sure that the Singapore Government never gets into situations when we make rosy projections which then suddenly run out of steam and, literally, regulatory and legislative panic breaks out.

sections.label: Sensitive question on integrity
sections.summary: The speaker declines to give a detailed answer, saying it is in Singapore's long-term strategic interests to have the rule of law and integrity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: That is a very sensitive question which I am not going to be able to give the Member a detailed answer to.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: It is in our long-term strategic interests to be above board, to be kosher, to have the rule of law and integrity being the hallmarks of our system.

sections.label: Singapore MFA punching above weight
sections.summary: Despite being a small country with a relatively small MFA budget, Singapore has punched above its weight internationally and is a large investor in China, Indonesia and India.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Not only is Singapore a small country, I think the MFA also has a relatively small budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Yet, despite that, it has punched well above its weight on the international stage, all the way from the Asia Pacific to the Arctic Circle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: I also understand that we are the largest investors for China, Indonesia and, I believe, second largest for India, the three most populous countries in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: And I think it is quite extraordinary that Singapore has managed to achieve all this, given its size and scale.
